item: Resume after an orphaned background task: the CLI's empty wake result draws NO summary line (2026-10-11)
branch: onResult: a result with num_turns === 0 that ends no request the page started (workStart 0, not busy) returns before the summary — the CLI emits one on --resume when a background task of the PREVIOUS process is reported (system/task_notification status:stopped → init → result num_turns 0, duration_ms 19, no tokens); a real turn's result (num_turns ≥ 1, or any result the page waited for) still draws the summary.
provenance: MEASURED 2026-10-11 on 2.1.296 over stdio: a bare `--resume` of a copy of a session whose previous process had left a background shell running emitted, at ~1.1 s and with no prompt, exactly these frames in this order (system/task_notification with summary "Background shell command didn't finish before the previous session ended", a replayed /model local-command user frame, system/init, result {num_turns:0, duration_ms:19, usage all 0, result:''}); stripping every queue-operation record from the copy changed nothing (the trigger is the CLI's task registry, not the transcript); a session with no orphaned task emits no result at all. The frames below are those tapes, trimmed. The user's screenshot: 'Resumed' then '✻ Pondered for 1s' (fmtDur floors at 1 s). Negative control RUN 2026-10-11 on the pre-fix build: 5/8 — step 1 drew one .done (expected 0), step 2 then counted 2, step 3 counted 3.

steps.note: 0 — a quiet page: no summary lines, not busy
1 — the resume-time triple (task_notification stopped → init → result num_turns 0): nothing is summarised

frames.summary: Background shell command didn't finish before the previous session ended

steps.note: 2 — a real turn still gets its summary: sendTurn-less wake shape with num_turns 1 after a streamed assistant
